t: The eastern Roman Empire, ruled from Constantinople, whose people called themselves Romans for over 1,100 years.
It preserved Roman law in Justinian's Code and Greek learning, and spread Orthodox Christianity to Russia and the Balkans.
Manzikert in 1071 and the crusader sack of 1204 crippled it; the Ottomans took Constantinople in 1453.
dyk: Hagia Sophia, completed under Justinian in 537, remained the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years.
ev: Constantine I dedicates Constantinople on the site of Byzantion
Death of Theodosius I divides the empire permanently into east and west
Leo III's Greek fire helps defeat the second Arab siege of Constantinople
Seljuk Turks defeat and capture Romanos IV Diogenes at Manzikert
The Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople and founds a Latin Empire
Michael VIII Palaiologos recovers Constantinople from the Latins
Mehmed II captures Constantinople; Constantine XI dies on the walls
